_note: Every threshold and weight the agent uses. Changed by a human,
reviewed, and benchmarked before it takes effect. The agent never
writes to this file and never adjusts a value at run time, per P1-C3
and P4-C8.

model._note: Local model served by Ollama over localhost. No hosted API.
model.name: llama3.1:8b-instruct-q4_K_M

input_limits._note: Checked at N2 so an oversized export fails with an instruction rather than an out-of-memory error, per P5-C7.

clustering._note: Events on one point separated by less than the gap belong to one condition.

nuisance._note: ISA-18.2 categories as recorded in docs/02_research_delta.md 2.2. Evaluated in this order; the first match is the classification applied.

preliminary_score._note: Alarm-side evidence only. Each term is a weight times a component normalised to 0..1, and the components are reported alongside the score.

reassessment._note: The N7 rule set from P0-C2. Quantities are multiples of the point's own deadband unless named otherwise, so one setting behaves the same on a temperature point and a pressure point.

_note: The electrical rule set, applied in N7 to conditions whose alarm class
is one of the signals below and to nothing else, so HVAC conditions keep
the six trend rules above. A cause confirmed by its trend ranks as the
item; a consequence that starts inside a confirmed cause's window, in
the scope the relation names, collapses under it. Relations are tried
in this order and the first match wins. Scope is any (anywhere in the
export), same_equipment, or upstream (equipment that feeds the cause,
from the journal's fed_from topology). Times are seconds before the
cause starts and after it ends. Trend evidence is read from the
condition's own span widened by evidence_margin_s on each side, since a
standby generator reads 0 Hz all day and that is not a frequency alarm.
A relation with root_cause false names a signal that is itself a
consequence and never ranks as a cause: it explains the listed
conditions only when it is confirmed and nothing explains it. LOAD_STEP
puts a generator frequency dip that starts while the load is on the
emergency source under an ATS transfer no utility failure accounts for.
How a generator frequency dip is measured. The dip is the load step,
so it is read from the transfer to the emergency source (the
load_step_signal) and only once the generator has reached rated
frequency, never across its run up from standstill. Without a
transfer it is read from the first sample at rated frequency after
start; with neither there is no measurement. Rated and recovered both
mean within tolerance_hz of nominal_hz. A transfer counts as this
dip's load step when it is within load_step_lookback_s before the dip.

signals.ats_transfer: ATS transfer to the emergency source

safety._note: Recommendations describe diagnostic steps. A control action verb in an N8 recommendation is a failed attempt, per P4-C1 and P2-C3. Every entry is an action. The noun 'setpoint' was removed on 2026-09-08: it blocked correct descriptive text about a setpoint point, and every way to actually change one is already caught by a verb here.

report._note: The operator marks an outcome per escalation; marked reports are saved to the feedback directory and retained, per P4-C4.

evaluation._note: Fixed 2026-09-03, before any holdout data was opened. Not revised after results are seen, per P5-C1.
